There’s been enough floating plant growth that more shrimp are comfortable hanging out up there. Snails have come to clean up the remaining fragments of the shrimp food. The rounded shells of several larger snails is making me suspect I have some bladder snails in my tank too. The repens are growing well behind the rock. The melting leaf of the crypt has quite a few holes in it today.

Day 16

Shrimp spotted eating a molt. This is a good sign! I thought I had seen some molts the past few days but I wasn’t sure. This one is definitely a...

Shrimp spotted eating a molt. This is a good sign! I thought I had seen some molts the past few days but I wasn’t sure. This one is definitely a head. This is very exciting. I’ve been stressing out about my water parameters and cycling, so this successful molt is huge. It means the tank conditions are good enough for them and as long as I keep things stable they should all survive.

Next milestone is breeding…I want to see eggs….

The lobelia in the front has a leaf that is wilting

Day 14

May 05, 2026

Saw a reddit post where Taiwan bee shrimp in hard tap water and they bred. So maybe everything is fine. 9 shrimps on the moss today. One of my shrimp...

Saw a reddit post where Taiwan bee shrimp in hard tap water and they bred. So maybe everything is fine. 9 shrimps on the moss today. One of my shrimp appears to be molting. It might not make it, but let’s see! They seemed stagnant and the snails were migrating to the top. I did a 30% water change with distilled water and fed them some shrimp food. A medium size shrimp claimed the pellet and chased off others trying to eat it. Gh - 5 Kh - 3 Turned down temp to 71. The shrimp from earlier that wasn’t moving is turning pink — but maybe not. The shrimps bellies have taken a pinkish tinge following the consumption of the food.

Day 13 - observations

May 04, 2026

Colony of around 10 that likes to stay on the right side of the tank. A couple reliable tank side crawlers. One floating plant surfer. Snail population continues to grow....

Colony of around 10 that likes to stay on the right side of the tank. A couple reliable tank side crawlers. One floating plant surfer. Snail population continues to grow. I spotted two new small ones today. There are at the very least 10 in the tank now, for that’s how much I could count with a cursory glance. They frequently graze the biofilm on the surface. Saw what looked like the detritus worms feasting on snail poop in the algae. A couple were on the surface too. A leaf came unplanted so I put it back. The repens in the back is growing leaves. I unblocked some of its light to give it a better chance. Speaking of the algae, tufts of it are not visible in the front. It’s become a network and foliage for my fauna. Floating plants continue to multiply. Roots are long and spiky.
